# `hearing_bill_links`

**Hearing-to-bill links**

One row per package revision, bill and link source, keyed by package_id, last_modified, bill_id and link source.

**Coverage.** Sampled. Bill references that the selected hearing packages' MODS records state on their cover. It does not show bills named only in constituent records, agendas, bill actions or transcript text, and does not measure recall; agenda acquisition remains deferred. *(measured 2026-09-28)*

**Data quality.** last_modified is the publisher package addition/update time, including metadata-only updates. Dated revisions remain in this table; date_issued and held_date do not replace that coordinate. A latest-package query selects one revision before current-document joins (see govinfo-revisions.md). Same-date rereads replace that revision explicitly; retained receipts and original captures keep prior evidence. mods_cover means held_on. The package measured confirmation on 19 of 20 cover pairs and 18 of 18 pairs where cover and agenda agreed. Agenda links mean noticed, not held_on: agenda-only pairs were confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16. Recall is unmeasured. Only 2 of 20 sampled House hearings and 0 of 3 Senate hearings stated COVER bills; a missing row does not establish that a hearing concerned no bills. A successfully re-read cover replaces only that package revision's prior links, including an empty result. Earlier revisions remain retained. Unread or refused bodies retain their prior links. held_date is the one date the hearing's MODS states. A compiled volume that states several dates has held_date NULL and every native date, in source order, in held_dates; the list does not establish that each bill was considered on each date. Before link rule d06e0bd80ca1 (2026-09-25) such a volume's links carried its first date (CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven), and rows not re-read since keep held_dates NULL. committee_system_code is the first of its hearing's hearing_transcripts.committee_system_codes, set again every run, so a link and its hearing state one committee key.

- **Parquet file:** `hearing_bill_links.parquet`
- **MCP `query_sql` support:** Configured; requires an available artifact.
- **Publication status:** Not established by this schema page or its measurement date.
- **Row count:** Not stated here; the MCP `describe_table` reply gives the live count under `publication`.

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package_id` | `VARCHAR` | The CHRG package the hearing was printed as, spelled exactly as `hearing_transcripts.package_id` is, which is this table's document key. |
| `congress` | `VARCHAR` | The numbered Congress, from the package id's own grammar. |
| `chamber` | `VARCHAR` | The chamber, from the package id's document-type code rather than from its first letter, the same rule `hearing_transcripts.chamber` uses. |
| `committee_system_code` | `VARCHAR` | The `authorityId` of the first `congCommittee` the package MODS names, already keyed the way `committees.system_code` is.  Half the join key a bill-side confirmation needs, and half the identity check an agenda row passed before it was written. |
| `held_date` | `VARCHAR` | The day the hearing was held, where the package MODS states one distinct `heldDate`; NULL where it states none or several (a compiled volume, whose dates are held_dates).  Not the day its transcript was issued.  The other half of the confirmation join key. |
| `event_id` | `VARCHAR` | The committee-meeting event id this link was reached through, so an agenda row joins `committee_meetings` and its own transcript row.  NULL on a cover row whose caller read no hearing detail: the MODS itself never states one. |
| `bill_id` | `VARCHAR` | `congress_bills.bill_id` for the measure, in the publisher's own type and number.  Part of the identity. |
| `link_id` | `VARCHAR` | Which rule in `interpretation/hearing_bill_links.py` stated this pair, from a sealed additions-only vocabulary: `mods_cover` (the package MODS's own cover list) and `docs_house_br` (the House Committee Repository's agenda) are implemented; `daily_digest_entry`, `congress_related_items` and `front_matter_designator` are measured, named and not yet filled.  Part of the identity, because two sources naming one pair is the evidence and collapsing them would delete it; additions-only because this value is published and a rename rewrites rows already out. |
| `relation` | `VARCHAR` | What the row asserts, from the sealed vocabulary `held_on` and `noticed`.  `mods_cover` rows are `held_on`, confirmed 19 of 20 by the bill's own action list; `docs_house_br` rows are `noticed`, because an agenda states intent and an agenda-only bill is confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16. |
| `evidence_text` | `VARCHAR` | The exact string the rule read, so a wrong row is readable without the record in hand: the MODS `context` marker on a cover row, and the `BILLS-118HR188ih.pdf` file name, the `legis-num` or the `description` on an agenda row. |
| `held_dates` | `VARCHAR[]` | Every nonempty `heldDate` the package MODS states, as a Native list in document order with repetitions kept; `[]` where it states none.  A compiled volume states several, and which bill was heard on which day is not stated, so no bill is paired with a date.  NULL on a row not re-read since the column was added (`mods_cover` 002). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct. |
| `last_modified` | `VARCHAR` | The parent hearing package's publisher modification timestamp. Joins the exact dated transcript revision; neither held_date nor link_rule_version supplies this source coordinate. |
